citation: The Sun and the New York Herald (New York), September 29, 1920, p. 1: 'EIGHT WHITE SOX INDICTED FOR THROWING 1919 SERIES; CICOTTE CONFESSES PLOT'.
describes_date: the 1919 World Series, and the Cook County grand jury's indictments of 28 September 1920
locator: Front page, the column headed 'EIGHT WHITE SOX INDICTED FOR THROWING 1919 SERIES', datelined Chicago, Sept. 28: the jury 'indicted seven White Sox players and one former member of the team for throwing the 1919 world's series to the Cincinnati Reds'; Cicotte's and Jackson's confessions; 'The White Sox players were fixed and paid before the series games were started.'
rights_note: A United States newspaper of 1920, out of copyright; digitized for Chronicling America.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-16 (T-2611) in the Library of Congress OCR text of the page (the resource's full-text file); quoted with the OCR's scanning errors corrected. The page image was not opened.
note: A New York paper reporting a Chicago grand jury the day after it sat, so tier 1 for the indictments and the confessions it prints, and for the fix as the jury and the confessions described it. Used for one time-stream caption on the way to 1904 (the year 1919); nothing in any scene is built from it.
what_it_supplies: that eight White Sox players (seven current, one former) were indicted on 28 September 1920 for throwing the 1919 World Series to Cincinnati
that Eddie Cicotte and Joe Jackson confessed to the grand jury
what_it_does_not_supply: the verdict: the trial came in 1921, after this issue
